maps.name: Searching the library catalogue
maps.context: A student uses a university library website on a laptop to find a book for an assignment.
maps.notes: Observed mappings come from a short peer walkthrough. Conceptualised mappings are possible interpretations to discuss or test further. The example stays focused on one simple interface task.

rows.description: Observed: The large rectangular field and the placeholder text suggest that the student can type a title or author.
signifiers: Placeholder text: Search books, articles, and more
Search icon at the right of the field

rows.description: Observed: The student expects pressing Enter to begin the search, and the interface supports that expectation.
signifiers: Search button sits beside the field

rows.description: Observed: The page shows the number of results and the current search term near the top of the results list.
Conceptualised: The filter categories could help narrow a large result set, but a new student may not know which category to use first.
rows.change: Test whether one recommended filter or a clearer ordering would help first-time users.

rows.description: Conceptualised: If every result card presents title, author, availability, and action in the same order, students can scan results more easily.
rows.change: Check whether the repeated card structure supports quick comparison.

rows.description: Conceptualised: A short loading response would reassure the student that the search has been received when results take longer to appear.
rows.change: Prototype a visible loading state and compare it with the current response.
